Amariah
ăm-ă-rī´ăh
n. pr. m. (Hebrew 'Amaryah, the LORD hath said)
Hebrew 'amar, to say, with Yah, the covenant name — the LORD hath said, or the LORD hath promised. Several men in Scripture bear it, most of them in the priestly line.

Biblical Definition

Amariah means the LORD hath said, and the men who bore it stand mostly in the high-priestly succession. The Chronicler places one between Meraioth and Ahitub: “Meraioth begat Amariah, and Amariah begat Ahitub” (1Ch 6:7), and another after Azariah: “And Azariah begat Amariah, and Amariah begat Ahitub” (1Ch 6:11). Ezra's own pedigree runs through the name: “The son of Amariah, the son of Azariah, the son of Meraioth” (Ezr 7:3). A Levite of Hebron's house bears it too: “Of the sons of Hebron; Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth” (1Ch 23:19). The most consequential Amariah is Jehoshaphat's chief priest, appointed over the ecclesiastical half of a divided jurisdiction: “And, behold, Amariah the chief priest is over you in all matters of the LORD; and Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah, for all the king's matters” (2Ch 19:11). And the name reaches the prophets: Zephaniah is the son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah, the son of Amariah (Zep 1:1).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) does not treat proper names of Scripture; the sense is given by the Hebrew, from 'amar, to say, and Yah, the LORD — the LORD hath said or promised.

expand to see more

AMARIAH. A Hebrew proper name; from amar, to say or promise, and Yah, the covenant name of God: the LORD hath said.

SAY, v.t. To speak; to utter in words; to declare.

PROMISE, n. In a general sense, a declaration, written or verbal, which binds the person who makes it, either in honor, conscience or law, to do or forbear a certain act.

Key Scripture

1Ch 6:7 — "Meraioth begat Amariah, and Amariah begat Ahitub,"

Ezr 7:3 — "The son of Amariah, the son of Azariah, the son of Meraioth,"

2Ch 19:11 — "And, behold, Amariah the chief priest is over you in all matters of the LORD; and Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah, for all the king's matters: also the Levites shall be officers before you. Deal courageously, and the LORD shall be with the good."

Zep 1:1 — "The word of the LORD which came unto Zephaniah the son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah, the son of Amariah, the son of Hizkiah, in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah."

Modern Corruption

Genealogies are dismissed as filler to be skipped, when the priestly lists are the documentary spine that makes a claim like Ezra's testable.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the evidentiary function of the registers. Ezra 7 does not assert that Ezra was a priest; it traces him, name by name, back through Amariah and Azariah and Meraioth to Aaron the chief priest. A man who could not produce the line was put from the priesthood as polluted, and Nehemiah 7 records it happening. The lists are the mechanism by which the office stayed accountable.

2 Chronicles 19:11 deserves separate notice for what it establishes about jurisdiction. Jehoshaphat placed Amariah the chief priest over all matters of the LORD and Zebadiah over all the king's matters. That is a real distinction of spheres inside one covenant nation — neither the modern secularist wall that silences the church in public, nor the fusion that makes the magistrate a bishop. The Reformers' two-kingdoms doctrine has an Old Testament precedent, and this verse is it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew 'Amaryah (H568), the LORD hath said; from 'amar (H559), to say, and the theophoric Yah (H3050), a shortened form of the covenant name.

expand to see more

Hebrew 'Amaryah (H568) — Amariah; 1 Chronicles 6:7, Ezra 7:3, 2 Chronicles 19:11.

Hebrew 'amar (H559) — to say, to promise; the verb in the name.

Hebrew Yah (H3050) — the shortened covenant name, borne in hundreds of Israelite names.

Hebrew kohen ha-rosh — chief priest; Amariah's office under Jehoshaphat.

Hebrew yachas (H3187) — to be reckoned by genealogy; the process the lists serve.

Usage

"“Amariah the chief priest is over you in all matters of the LORD” — jurisdiction, defined."

"“The son of Amariah, the son of Azariah” — Ezra's credentials, traceable to Aaron."

"The name means the LORD hath said; it is borne mostly by men who handled what He said."
